root_cause.text: The st_lsm6dsx IIO buffer setup exposed the FIFO sampling-frequency sysfs attribute for all sensor types, but the ODR validation code indexed a 2-entry `odr_table` by `sensor->id`, causing an out-of-bounds access when non-accelerometer/non-gyroscope sensors wrote that attribute.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `st_lsm6dsx_fifo_setup()` to pass `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs` only for `ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC` and `NULL` for other sensors, with the comment explaining that only accelerometer events need this feature; the CVE text states `st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store()` calls `st_lsm6dsx_check_odr()`, which accesses `odr_table[sensor->id]` even though the array has only 2 entries.

intent_record.intent_summary: Enable accelerometer-specific FIFO sampling configuration by passing custom buffer attributes only for the accelerometer.
intent_record.what: In st_lsm6dsx_fifo_setup(), a new local pointer variable `attrs` was introduced inside the loop. For each enabled IIO device, `attrs` is set to `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs` only when `i == ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC`, and to `NULL` for all other sensor types. The call to `devm_iio_kfifo_buffer_setup_ext()` was changed to pass `attrs` instead of always passing `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs`. A comment was added explaining the accelerometer-specific behavior.
intent_record.how: This makes FIFO buffer setup apply the custom attribute set only to the accelerometer. As a result, accelerometer FIFO sampling frequency can be configured independently of the sensor sampling frequency, allowing higher accelerometer sampling rates while keeping FIFO data rate lower for event detection. Other sensors no longer receive those attributes through this setup path.

grouping_result.intent: Enable accelerometer-specific FIFO sampling configuration by passing custom buffer attributes only for the accelerometer.

relevance_review.reason: The change restricts the FIFO sampling-frequency buffer attribute to accelerometer sensors only, which directly addresses the root cause where the attribute was incorrectly exposed to all sensor types and could trigger out-of-bounds ODR table indexing.

candidates.rationale: This setup call installs the same custom buffer attributes for every IIO device in the loop, which exposed the FIFO sampling-frequency sysfs attribute to non-accelerometer/non-gyroscope sensors and allowed them to hit the ODR validation path that indexes the 2-entry table by sensor->id.

vuln_statements.explanation: This buffer setup call was applied in the per-device loop and exposed the custom FIFO sampling-frequency sysfs attribute to all sensor types, not just accelerometer/gyroscope devices. That exposure let unsupported sensors reach the ODR validation path that later indexed the 2-entry odr_table by sensor->id, causing the out-of-bounds access.

    The rate at which accelerometer or gyroscope sensor samples are fed
    to the hardware FIFO (batch data rate, or BDR) does not have to
    coincide with the sensor sampling frequency (output data rate, or
    ODR); the only requirement is for the BDR to not be greater than

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is not present in this snippet. The root cause was that the FIFO buffer sysfs sampling_frequency attribute was exposed to all sensor types, and ODR validation indexed a 2-entry table by `sensor->id`, causing out-of-bounds access for non-accel/gyro sensors. In this commit, the buffer sysfs attribute is added via `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs[] = { &iio_dev_attr_sampling_frequency, NULL }`, but the actual store handler validates against the current sensor ODR and the new buffer ODR state: `ret = st_lsm6dsx_check_odr(sensor, hwfifo_odr, &data);` followed by `if (hwfifo_odr <= sensor->odr) sensor->hwfifo_odr_mHz = hwfifo_odr; else ret = -EINVAL;`. The code also switches FIFO-related logic away from `sensor->odr` to `sensor->hwfifo_odr_mHz` in several places. There is no visible indexing of an ODR table by `sensor->id` in this function body, and the fix to separate buffer ODR from sensor ODR is already present.
